The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found one real defect and no missing requirements. All 176 tests pass, and every acceptance criterion in #7 has a test whose name says which criterion it covers.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial:** nothing. I checked each criterion against the code and the tests:\n- **Lifecycle:** create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete all work. Delete goes through a confirmation screen (GET) before the POST.\n- **Slugs:** pages reuse the post slug rules (`_slug_for(conn, \"pages\", …)`, `app/content.py:268-274`) and refuse the four reserved names whether typed or made from the title. The slug locks once the page is first published.\n- **Vista previa:** uses the same `markdown.to_html` as posts.\n- **Access:** all 10 page routes are declared leader-only in `app/policy.py:21-31`, so the existing access-control test in `tests/test_t01_access.py` covers them automatically.\n- **Export and menu:** pages are written at the site root, and every public page's menu lists *Inicio* then published pages in menu order. Draft pages appear nowhere.\n- **Seed:** the four pages are published in order, with the house rules and `unete@albiazul.example`.\n\n**(c) Implemented but wrong:**\n- **The dashboard post counts no longer match the list they open (leader only).** Spec: *\"the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts…\"*. The T04 test is named `test_each_dashboard_count_opens_the_content_list_filtered_to_that_status`.\n  - The counts still cover posts only (`count_by_status`). But the leader's unfiltered content list now mixes posts and pages (`app/routes/posts.py:109-112`), and the count links only add `status=` (`templates/admin/dashboard.html:10`).\n  - I confirmed it against a temp database with one published post, one published page and one draft page. *Publicadas* shows **1** but opens a list of 2 rows (the post and *Quiénes somos*). *Borradores* shows **0** but opens a list with *Borrador de página*.\n  - The T04 test still passes only because it never creates a page. The likely fix is to add `type=post` to those links for the leader, and extend the test to include a page.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (minor, all defensible):**\n- **Menu order limited to 0–999.** The spec only says *\"a menu-order number\"*, but the code refuses anything else (`app/content.py:417-422`, `templates/admin/page_form.html:30`), with a parametrized test. It's reasonable validation; I'm noting it as an invented rule.\n- **The 404 page now names what's missing.** `NotFound` gained a `missing` parameter (`app/web.py:43`, `templates/admin/not_found.html:4`), so a missing page says \"esa página\" instead of \"esa publicación\". It's a small change outside pages proper.\n- **The leader's default content list changed.** Its heading is now \"Publicaciones y páginas\" and it shows pages without any filter (`templates/admin/content.html:2-3`), plus there's a new *Páginas* link in the admin menu. The spec's *\"(leader only) post vs page\"* filter implies a mixed list, so this is fine, but it is what causes the finding in (c).\n\nNothing else I found goes beyond what was asked.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>91731</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>13</tool_uses><duration_ms>123283</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"parentUuid":"a0f2e5bf-4bfd-4866-a470-957917ae4eb7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"73dd9d66-131a-4feb-a3ae-70a5f2907b6e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.4.1/skills/receiving-code-review\n\n# Code Review Reception\n\n## Overview\n\nCode review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.\n\n**Core principle:** Verify before implementing. Ask before assuming. Technical correctness over social comfort.\n\n## The Response Pattern\n\n```\nWHEN receiving code review feedback:\n\n1. READ: Complete feedback without reacting\n2. UNDERSTAND: Restate requirement in own words (or ask)\n3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality\n4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?\n5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback\n6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each\n```\n\n## Forbidden Responses\n\n**NEVER:**\n- \"You're absolutely right!\" (explicit instruction-file violation)\n- \"Great point!\" / \"Excellent feedback!\" (performative)\n- \"Let me implement that now\" (before verification)\n\n**INSTEAD:**\n- Restate the technical requirement\n- Ask clarifying questions\n- Push back with technical reasoning if wrong\n- Just start working (actions > words)\n\n## Handling Unclear Feedback\n\n```\nIF any item is unclear:\n  STOP - do not implement anything yet\n  ASK for clarification on unclear items\n\nWHY: Items may be related. Partial understanding = wrong implementation.\n```\n\n**Example:**\n```\nyour human partner: \"Fix 1-6\"\nYou understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.\n\n❌ WRONG: Implement 1,2,3,6 now, ask about 4,5 later\n✅ RIGHT: \"I understand items 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before proceeding.\"\n```\n\n## Source-Specific Handling\n\n### From your human partner\n- **Trusted** - implement after understanding\n- **Still ask** if scope unclear\n- **No performative agreement**\n- **Skip to action** or technical acknowledgment\n\n### From External Reviewers\n```\nBEFORE implementing:\n  1. Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase?\n  2. Check: Breaks existing functionality?\n  3. Check: Reason for current implementation?\n  4. Check: Works on all platforms/versions?\n  5. Check: Does reviewer understand full context?\n\nIF suggestion seems wrong:\n  Push back with technical reasoning\n\nIF can't easily verify:\n  Say so: \"I can't verify this without [X]. Should I [investigate/ask/proceed]?\"\n\nIF conflicts with your human partner's prior decisions:\n  Stop and discuss with your human partner first\n```\n\n**your human partner's rule:** \"External feedback - be skeptical, but check carefully\"\n\n## YAGNI Check for \"Professional\" Features\n\n```\nIF reviewer suggests \"implementing properly\":\n  grep codebase for actual usage\n\n  IF unused: \"This endpoint isn't called. Remove it (YAGNI)?\"\n  IF used: Then implement properly\n```\n\n**your human partner's rule:** \"You and reviewer both report to me. If we don't need this feature, don't add it.\"\n\n## Implementation Order\n\n```\nFOR multi-item feedback:\n  1. Clarify anything unclear FIRST\n  2. Then implement in this order:\n     - Blocking issues (breaks, security)\n     - Simple fixes (typos, imports)\n     - Complex fixes (refactoring, logic)\n  3. Test each fix individually\n  4. Verify no regressions\n```\n\n## When To Push Back\n\nPush back when:\n- Suggestion breaks existing functionality\n- Reviewer lacks full context\n- Violates YAGNI (unused feature)\n- Technically incorrect for this stack\n- Legacy/compatibility reasons exist\n- Conflicts with your human partner's architectural decisions\n\n**How to push back:**\n- Use technical reasoning, not defensiveness\n- Ask specific questions\n- Reference working tests/code\n- Involve your human partner if architectural\n\n**If you're uncomfortable pushing back out loud:** Name that tension, then tell your partner about the issue you've seen. They'll appreciate your honesty.\n\n## Acknowledging Correct Feedback\n\nWhen feedback IS correct:\n```\n✅ \"Fixed. [Brief description of what changed]\"\n✅ \"Good catch - [specific issue]. Fixed in [location].\"\n✅ [Just fix it and show in the code]\n\n❌ \"You're absolutely right!\"\n❌ \"Great point!\"\n❌ \"Thanks for catching that!\"\n❌ \"Thanks for [anything]\"\n❌ ANY gratitude expression\n```\n\n**Why no thanks:** Actions speak. Just fix it. The code itself shows you heard the feedback.\n\n**If you catch yourself about to write \"Thanks\":** DELETE IT. State the fix instead.\n\n## Gracefully Correcting Your Pushback\n\nIf you pushed back and were wrong:\n```\n✅ \"You were right - I checked [X] and it does [Y]. Implementing now.\"\n✅ \"Verified this and you're correct. My initial understanding was wrong because [reason]. Fixing.\"\n\n❌ Long apology\n❌ Defending why you pushed back\n❌ Over-explaining\n```\n\nState the correction factually and move on.\n\n## Common Mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n|---------|-----|\n| Performative agreement | State requirement or just act |\n| Blind implementation | Verify against codebase first |\n| Batch without testing | One at a time, test each |\n| Assuming reviewer is right | Check if breaks things |\n| Avoiding pushback | Technical correctness > comfort |\n| Partial implementation | Clarify all items first |\n| Can't verify, proceed anyway | State limitation, ask for direction |\n\n## Real Examples\n\n**Performative Agreement (Bad):**\n```\nReviewer: \"Remove legacy code\"\n❌ \"You're absolutely right! Let me remove that...\"\n```\n\n**Technical Verification (Good):**\n```\nReviewer: \"Remove legacy code\"\n✅ \"Checking... build target is 10.15+, this API needs 13+. Need legacy for backward compat. Current impl has wrong bundle ID - fix it or drop pre-13 support?\"\n```\n\n**YAGNI (Good):**\n```\nReviewer: \"Implement proper metrics tracking with database, date filters, CSV export\"\n✅ \"Grepped codebase - nothing calls this endpoint. Remove it (YAGNI)? Or is there usage I'm missing?\"\n```\n\n**Unclear Item (Good):**\n```\nyour human partner: \"Fix items 1-6\"\nYou understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.\n✅ \"Understand 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before implementing.\"\n```\n\n## GitHub Thread Replies\n\nWhen replying to inline review comments on GitHub, reply in the comment thread (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{id}/replies`), not as a top-level PR comment.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"00c2fd79-b296-4f34-a54b-436d84d66864","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:15:33.335Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01VGPrsnw57r79yoCzr4NoV3","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"660bc2b9-6920-42a9-963a-9574f3879318","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

All 176 tests pass, and every acceptance criterion in #7 has a test whose name says which criterion it covers.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial:** nothing. I checked each criterion against the code and the tests:\n- **Lifecycle:** create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete all work. Delete goes through a confirmation screen (GET) before the POST.\n- **Slugs:** pages reuse the post slug rules (`_slug_for(conn, \"pages\", …)`, `app/content.py:268-274`) and refuse the four reserved names whether typed or made from the title. The slug locks once the page is first published.\n- **Vista previa:** uses the same `markdown.to_html` as posts.\n- **Access:** all 10 page routes are declared leader-only in `app/policy.py:21-31`, so the existing access-control test in `tests/test_t01_access.py` covers them automatically.\n- **Export and menu:** pages are written at the site root, and every public page's menu lists *Inicio* then published pages in menu order. Draft pages appear nowhere.\n- **Seed:** the four pages are published in order, with the house rules and `unete@albiazul.example`.\n\n**(c) Implemented but wrong:**\n- **The dashboard post counts no longer match the list they open (leader only).** Spec: *\"the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts…\"*. The T04 test is named `test_each_dashboard_count_opens_the_content_list_filtered_to_that_status`.\n  - The counts still cover posts only (`count_by_status`). But the leader's unfiltered content list now mixes posts and pages (`app/routes/posts.py:109-112`), and the count links only add `status=` (`templates/admin/dashboard.html:10`).\n  - I confirmed it against a temp database with one published post, one published page and one draft page. *Publicadas* shows **1** but opens a list of 2 rows (the post and *Quiénes somos*). *Borradores* shows **0** but opens a list with *Borrador de página*.\n  - The T04 test still passes only because it never creates a page. The likely fix is to add `type=post` to those links for the leader, and extend the test to include a page.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (minor, all defensible):**\n- **Menu order limited to 0–999.** The spec only says *\"a menu-order number\"*, but the code refuses anything else (`app/content.py:417-422`, `templates/admin/page_form.html:30`), with a parametrized test. It's reasonable validation; I'm noting it as an invented rule.\n- **The 404 page now names what's missing.** `NotFound` gained a `missing` parameter (`app/web.py:43`, `templates/admin/not_found.html:4`), so a missing page says \"esa página\" instead of \"esa publicación\". It's a small change outside pages proper.\n- **The leader's default content list changed.** Its heading is now \"Publicaciones y páginas\" and it shows pages without any filter (`templates/admin/content.html:2-3`), plus there's a new *Páginas* link in the admin menu. The spec's *\"(leader only) post vs page\"* filter implies a mixed list, so this is fine, but it is what causes the finding in (c).\n\nNothing else I found goes beyond what was asked.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>91731</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>13</tool_uses><duration_ms>123283</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>","reason":"absorbed_mid_turn","commandUuid":"a7348297-b947-40f3-a7fd-3e7b3fb3798c","deliveryId":"742a6bee-ee25-4e02-9db3-082655fe8597"}

But the leader's unfiltered content list now mixes posts and pages (`app/routes/posts.py:109-112`), and the count links only add `status=` (`templates/admin/dashboard.html:10`).\n  - I confirmed it against a temp database with one published post, one published page and one draft page. *Publicadas* shows **1** but opens a list of 2 rows (the post and *Quiénes somos*). *Borradores* shows **0** but opens a list with *Borrador de página*.\n  - The T04 test still passes only because it never creates a page. {"parentUuid":"c00efaa6-dda9-4c3b-9cd8-f7744db28e67","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"73dd9d66-131a-4feb-a3ae-70a5f2907b6e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/domain-modeling\n\n# Domain Modeling\n\nActively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)\n\n## File structure\n\nMost repos have a single context:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/\n│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nIf a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n├── src/\n│   ├── ordering/\n│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions\n│   └── billing/\n│       ├── CONTEXT.md\n│       └── docs/adr/\n```\n\nCreate files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.\n\n## During the session\n\n### Challenge against the glossary\n\nWhen the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. \"Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?\"\n\n### Sharpen fuzzy language\n\nWhen the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. \"You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things.\"\n\n### Discuss concrete scenarios\n\nWhen domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.\n\n### Cross-reference with code\n\nWhen the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: \"Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?\"\n\n### Update CONTEXT.md inline\n\nWhen a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).\n\n`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.\n\n### Offer ADRs sparingly\n\nOnly offer to create an ADR when all three are true:\n\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder \"why did they do it this way?\"\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\n\nIf any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Small glossary update for T06: Page now has a menu order and draft/published only; Slug applies to pages too, with reserved names."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"c8b2f5f3-0f07-4c6e-a4fc-409620718e32","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:18:20.392Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01DnikovqufPLF7BdBvRK3jM","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"660bc2b9-6920-42a9-963a-9574f3879318","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"d2a34e38-7000-49a7-9629-2e6a5c010b43","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfvqEV11n71CHB6V9UPBH","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VFgdQXn3mLdT6KVfveaBXD","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"gh issue comment 7 --body-file - <<'EOF'\n## `/code-review` findings for T06 and how each was resolved\n\nThe review compared uncommitted work against `2f025cb` along two separate axes, each run by its own sub-agent.\n\n### Spec (against this ticket's acceptance criteria and spec #1)\n\nNothing is missing. Every acceptance criterion maps to a test whose name says which criterion it covers.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Wrong behaviour.** On the leader's dashboard, *Borradores* and *Publicadas* count posts only, but their links opened a list that also held pages. With one draft page, *Borradores* showed 0 and opened a list with that page in it. | **Fixed.** The four post counts now link with `type=post`. New test: `test_each_dashboard_post_count_still_opens_just_the_posts_it_counts_when_there_are_pages`. The link readers in the tests (`dashboard_counts` in conftest, and the T04 link test) now read `&amp;` in an href as `&`, the way a browser does; this was needed once a link carries two parameters. |\n| 2 | **Not asked for:** menu order is limited to 0–999. | **Kept.** SQLite cannot store an integer of any length; a very long number would crash the save instead of showing a message. The editor's help text states the range. Covered by `test_page_menu_order_must_be_a_whole_number_from_0_to_999`. |\n| 3 | **Not asked for:** the 404 page names what is missing. | **Kept.** Without it, a missing page would say \"No encontramos esa publicación\", calling a page a post (see CONTEXT.md). |\n| 4 | **Not asked for:** the leader's unfiltered content list mixes posts and pages. | **Kept.** Spec #1's \"(leader only) post vs page\" filter implies a mixed list. Finding 1 fixed its side effect. |\n\n### Standards (CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, ADRs, and the code-smell baseline)\n\nThere are no hard violations: links are relative, every form carries a CSRF token, Markdown is sanitized in both *Vista previa* and the export, and drafts stay out of the export. Every page route is declared leader-only, and no dependency was added.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | The seed pages called Rayados \"el club\", which CONTEXT.md lists under _Avoid_. | **Fixed.** Now \"No somos Rayados ni hablamos por el equipo\" and \"los publica Rayados\". |\n| 2 | Post vs page had several names (`kind`, `type`, `CONTENT_TYPES`, *Tipo*), and `kind` is on Topic's _Avoid_ list. The glossary had no menu order, and Slug was defined for posts only. | **Fixed.** The route parameter is now `content_type`; the query string stays `type`, as the spec's route contract says. CONTEXT.md: Page gains *Página* and its draft/published life, Slug now covers pages and the names the site already uses, and **Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*) is new. |\n| 3 | Templates checked `user.is_leader` instead of asking Policy. | **Fixed for the new code.** `may_manage_pages` is now a template global, used by the admin menu and the content list. The existing *Cuentas* link is outside this ticket and was left as it was. |\n| 4 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `saved_message` existed in both the post and page routes. | **Fixed.** Both now call one `web.saved_message(..., taken_by)`. |\n| 5 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `take_action` exists in both route modules. | **Kept.** Each re-renders a different screen; sharing it would need a render callback to save about 8 lines. |\n| 6 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `typed_slug`, `slug_locked` and `status_name` are repeated on `Page` and `Post`. | **Kept.** They are two-line properties on flat, frozen dataclasses; a shared base class would add inheritance for little gain. |\n| 7 | `content.html` hard-coded the type names when `types` was already passed in. | **Fixed.** It now uses `types[type]`. |\n| 8 | The T06 tests copy helpers from the T02 and T03 tests. | **Kept.** Each test file defines its own small helpers here (T04 also has its own `text`); moving them to conftest would mean editing earlier tickets' tests. |\n| 9 | Smell, Primitive Obsession: a table name passed as `table: str` into SQL built with an f-string. | **Fixed.** It is now typed `Table = Literal[\"posts\", \"pages\"]`, so only those two names can reach the SQL; mypy checks it. |\n| 10 | Smell, Repeated Switches: the code branches on post vs page in several places. | **Kept.** They are three single branches in different layers: the filter, the table row, and the Jinja test. |\n| 11 | Smell, Mysterious Name: `_validate_page` also returned the menu order. | **Fixed.** It only validates now, like `_validate` does for posts. |\n| 12 | Smell, Mysterious Name: a boolean was called `pages`, and the menu loop variable was `entry`. | **Fixed.** They are now `sees_pages` and `menu_page`. |\n| 13 | The `posts.py` docstring was stale, and the `export.py` docstring was ambiguous. | **Fixed.** Both reworded. |\n\n**Verification:** `uv run pytest` gives 177 passed (149 before this ticket). `mypy app scripts/seed_demo.py` reports no issues.\nEOF","description":"Post code review findings as a comment on issue 7"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1932,"cache_read_input_tokens":238508,"output_tokens":2246,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":177},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1932,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2246,"cache_read_input_tokens":238508,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1932,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1932},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01VFgdQXn3mLdT6KVfveaBXD":{"command":"cd a shared base class would add inheritance for little gain. |\n| 7 | `content.html` hard-coded the type names when `types` was already passed in. | **Fixed.** It now uses `types[type]`. |\n| 8 | The T06 tests copy helpers from the T02 and T03 tests. | **Kept.** Each test file defines its own small helpers here (T04 also has its own `text`); moving them to conftest would mean editing earlier tickets' tests. |\n| 9 | Smell, Primitive Obsession: a table name passed as `table: str` into SQL built with an f-string. | **Fixed.** It is now typed `Table = Literal[\"posts\", \"pages\"]`, so only those two names can reach the SQL; mypy checks it. |\n| 10 | Smell, Repeated Switches: the code branches on post vs page in several places. | **Kept.** They are three single branches in different layers: the filter, the table row, and the Jinja test. |\n| 11 | Smell, Mysterious Name: `_validate_page` also returned the menu order. | **Fixed.** It only validates now, like `_validate` does for posts. |\n| 12 | Smell, Mysterious Name: a boolean was called `pages`, and the menu loop variable was `entry`. | **Fixed.** They are now `sees_pages` and `menu_page`. |\n| 13 | The `posts.py` docstring was stale, and the `export.py` docstring was ambiguous. | **Fixed.** Both reworded. |\n\n**Verification:** `uv run pytest` gives 177 passed (149 before this ticket). `mypy app scripts/seed_demo.py` reports no issues.\nEOF","description":"Post code review findings as a comment on issue 7"}},"wireIngestContext":{"toolu_01VFgdQXn3mLdT6KVfveaBXD":{"cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfvqEUgv9hLNjxxobCcYN","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"27fb7617-57d4-401a-8b16-04e2a2890cec","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:19:43.695Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"660bc2b9-6920-42a9-963a-9574f3879318","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"0dd3be50-6e6c-4218-b9d0-bb25d60e1602","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfvqGevsaf4KFpgcqkSeg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Ticket #7 (T06) is done and committed to `main` as `196f321`, but not pushed. The issue will close itself when you push, because the commit ends with `Closes #7`.\n\n**What the leader can do now**\n- Create, edit, preview, publish, unpublish and delete pages; deleting asks for confirmation first.\n- Pages follow the same slug rules as posts. They can't take the names `index`, `tema`, `posts` or `style`, and the slug stops changing once the page is first published.\n- Every page route is leader-only. Members never see pages, either in their admin menu or in their content list, even if they type `?type=page`.\n- The export writes each published page at the site root. Every public page's menu shows *Inicio*, then the published pages in menu order. Draft and unpublished pages appear nowhere.\n- The leader's content list shows posts and pages together, with a filter for one or the other. The dashboard shows a page count.\n- The seed publishes *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa* and *Cómo unirse*, in that order.\n\n**Verification:** 177 tests pass (149 before, 28 new). The project has no type checker set up, so I ran mypy once through `uvx`, without adding a dependency; it found no issues.\n\n**Code review:** the review ran in two separate parts:\n- **Spec** (does it do what #7 asks): it found one real bug. On the leader's dashboard, *Borradores* and *Publicadas* count posts only, but their links opened a list that also included pages. I fixed it test-first; the links now filter to posts.\n- **Standards** (does it follow the repo's rules): no hard violations. I fixed the soft ones, which included:\n  - The seed pages called Rayados \"el club\", a word `CONTEXT.md` says to avoid.\n  - A shared slug message was duplicated between posts and pages.\n  - The new templates checked the role directly instead of asking Policy.\n  - The new code used several different names for post vs page.\n\nA few duplication findings I kept on purpose, with reasons. Every finding and its resolution is posted on #7.\n\n**Changes outside the new page code:**\n- **T04 tests:** two dashboard tests checked the exact set of counts, so I added *Páginas* to them, the same way T05 added *Cambios propuestos*.\n- **Link reading in tests:** the dashboard links now carry two query parameters, so the test helpers that follow them read `&amp;` as `&`, the way a browser does.\n- **Glossary:** `CONTEXT.md` gains a **Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*) entry, and its Page and Slug entries now cover pages.\n- **Menu-order limit:** menu order only accepts whole numbers from 0 to 999. The spec doesn't say this; without a limit, a very long number would crash the save.\n\nI left your other uncommitted changes (`.gitignore`, `notes/`, `docs/transcripts/`) out of the commit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":657,"cache_read_input_tokens":243858,"output_tokens":1040,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":66},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":657,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1040,"cache_read_input_tokens":243858,"cache_creation_input_tokens":657,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":657},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfvqGeChqCByMK3a9YNfC","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"b89ac720-27fe-41f0-9178-40afaaa155bd","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:20:04.433Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"660bc2b9-6920-42a9-963a-9574f3879318","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"1980206b-59f7-4b43-9b94-1420f89727c3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b14ec820-b739-45ef-aa63-491ad50f0bfe","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SAps7T8eLtoHtRsB6TottW","type":"tool_result","content":"#8 T07: The leader manages accounts; members choose a nickname and change their password\n## Parent\n#1\n## What to build\n## Acceptance criteria\n- [ ] The leader creates an account with a unique email, a role and a temporary password of at least 8 characters; the new user has no nickname yet.\n- [ ] A user without a nickname is redirected from every admin route to the nickname screen until they choose one: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case. Afterwards a member cannot change it.\n- [ ] The leader can change any user's role, set any user's nickname (still unique) and set a new temporary password.\n- [ ] The leader can deactivate and reactivate accounts. A deactivated user cannot log in, and an open session of a deactivated user is rejected on its next request.\n- [ ] The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate themselves; the attempt is refused with a message.\n- [ ] Users are never deleted. A deactivated member's published posts stay in the export under their nickname, and their submitted posts stay in the review queue.\n- [ ] On *Mi cuenta* any user changes their own password by giving the current one and a new one of at least 8 characters; it is stored as an argon2 hash.\n- [ ] Every user-management route is leader-only and covered by the access-control test.\n- [ ] The dashboard shows the number of active members.\n## Blocked by\nBlocked by: #2, #4\n\n#9 T08: The leader updates the site with one button, and the site gets its final look\n## Parent\n#1\n## What to build\n## Acceptance criteria\n- [ ] A leader-only *Actualizar el sitio* POST (with CSRF token) runs the export and then the upload, and reports each step (*\"Sitio generado ✓ · Subido a GitHub ✓\"*); if the upload fails it shows a plain Spanish error and the successful export still counts.\n- [ ] The time of the last successful export is recorded and shown on the dashboard.\n- [ ] Tests replace the upload with a fake; no test pushes to GitHub. Members get 403 (access-control test).\n- [ ] `uv run cms publish` and `uv run cms deploy` still work as before.\n- [ ] The home page has an original inline Cerro de la Silla banner and every public page has a generic stadium silhouette above the disclaimer; no image files, crest, logos or photos are used.\n- [ ] Manual: no horizontal overflow at 390 px on the public home page, the dashboard, the content list and the post editor.\n- [ ] The seed matches the spec's demo data list and runs clean from `.env.example` values.\n## Blocked by\nBlocked by: #6, #7, #8","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"6ed11811-f92b-4d7b-a8be-580f69e88ae5","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:20:39.839Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"#8 T07: The leader manages accounts; members choose a nickname and change their password\n## Parent\n#1\n## What to build\n## Acceptance criteria\n- [ ] The leader creates an account with a unique email, a role and a temporary password of at least 8 characters; the new user has no nickname yet.\n- [ ] A user without a nickname is redirected from every admin route to the nickname screen until they choose one: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case.
